source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
During the first one to two years after planting, before the tree has flowered, the top priority is establishing a strong, evenly-branched canopy and root system. Water consistently and do not let the young tree dry out or wilt for extended periods, since repeated wilting stress at this stage stunts the tree and delays first fruiting.

After planting, growers should mulch generously around the root zone with straw, rice husk, or dried leaves, refreshing the mulch as it breaks down; this both conserves soil moisture and suppresses weeds that would otherwise compete with the shallow young roots. A shallow-rooted young durian benefits from partial shade in its first year or two -- full, harsh sun on a very young seedling can scorch leaves and slow establishment -- but shade should be gradually reduced as the tree matures toward its bearing years, since a mature durian is a full-sun tree.

Weeding: keep the area under the canopy free of weeds and grass, particularly right around the trunk base, since dense weed growth both competes for water/nutrients and keeps humidity high against the bark, which favors collar and root disease.
